dd3b8b08b9ef241b039249c3567a4f9376c32d32.summary: A 2015 blog post describes CryptoFortress ransomware. The author began hunting for Gootkit, found a Nuclear Pack instance in France pushing CryptoFortress via CVE-2013-2551 on 2015-03-04, and first took the sample for Teerac.A (aka TorrentLocker). The sample then showed a close identity with CryptoFortress. The author says the post was heavily edited to fix a mistake. Two samples are listed, and the post cites an ESET TorrentLocker report and a CertLexsi CryptoFortress reading.

dd292ad0fef27eff1a38732bf4629f566c3534f7.summary: ESET published research on 21 previously undocumented Linux malware families that backdoor OpenSSH, dated 5 December 2018. Most families include a credential-stealing feature and a backdoor mode. The report highlights Kessel, Kamino, Chandrila and Bonadan. Kamino was first used by a DarkLeech-linked crimeware campaign and later appeared in attacks on Russian banks by a group ESET cites as Carbanak. Samples were found using YARA rules derived from an earlier Windigo detection script, plus a custom honeypot.
